eyebrow: Creating a private registry inside Azure itself
caption: Real Azure Portal screen for creating a Container Registry -- it lives inside Northbridge's own subscription, authenticated by the same Azure identity as the rest of their infrastructure.

code:
$ az acr create --resource-group northbridge-rg \
  --name northbridgeacr --sku Basic
$ az acr login --name northbridgeacr
Login Succeeded

$ docker tag northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5 \
  northbridgeacr.azurecr.io/catalog:1.5
$ docker push northbridgeacr.azurecr.io/catalog:1.5
caption: az acr login authenticates Docker using the already-signed-in Azure CLI session -- no separate registry password.

eyebrow: A pushed image, visible in the registry
caption: Real Azure Portal Repositories view -- a pushed image shows up here exactly like it would on Docker Hub's repository page, just inside Northbridge's own Azure subscription.

eyebrow: Pushing to Amazon ECR, for checkout's ECS deploy
code:
$ aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | \
  docker login --username AWS --password-stdin \
  123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Login Succeeded

$ docker tag northbridgeretail/checkout:2.1 \
  123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/checkout:2.1
$ docker push 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/checkout:2.1
caption: aws ecr get-login-password returns a 12-hour token piped straight into docker login -- same authenticate-tag-push shape, AWS's own credentials instead.
